title: Exhaustive Pattern Matching on Public Structs
pattern: A library defines a public struct with all public fields without restricting pattern matching, exposing it to exhaustive destructuring by clients.
why_bad: Adding a new private or public field to the struct in a future library update will instantly break compilation of all downstream client code because their pattern matches are no longer exhaustive.
detection: A public struct is declared with all public fields and lacks the `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute, allowing external pattern matches.
counterexample: An external library uses `#[non_exhaustive]` on public structs or keeps at least one field private.
fix: Add the `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute to the struct: `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct Config { pub dry_run: bool }`.
